sources.title: Kreemer, Haines, Holt, Blewitt & Lavallée (2000), 'On the determination of a global strain rate model', Earth Planets Space 52(10):765–770, doi:10.1186/BF03352279
sources.used_for: THE Stage-A formula. Eq. (2) average seismic strain rate from moment tensors; Eq. (3) the fault-slip variant: eps_ij = (1/2A) * sum_k (L_k * u_k / sin(dip_k)) * m_ij, with n fault segments in grid area A, length L_k, dip dip_k, slip rate u_k and unit moment tensor m_ij.
sources.verified: SELF (PDF text with both equations retrieved and read 2026-10-06; the same equations are restated in GJI 212(2):988 and GJI 146(2):399)
sources.license: Author/UNR-hosted PDF; cite the journal article.
sources.notes: The brief asked for a documented moment-tensor summation with its source. This is it, line by line: sum(L*u/sin dip) over 2A, contracted with the unit moment tensor. src/gems51/strain.py implements the scalar contraction and says so.

sources.title: Zeng & Shen (2016), 'A fault-based model for crustal deformation, fault slip rates and off-fault strain rate in California', BSSA 106(2):766–784, doi:10.1785/0120140250
sources.used_for: Physical premise that a large, spatially structured moment budget is NOT carried by mapped faults (the Stage-A deficit idea).
sources.verified: OWNER + SELF (USGS Publications Warehouse record fetched earlier in this session; the abstract states the off-fault moment rate)
sources.notes: Treated as motivation, not as a result: the deficit is measured here (median 0.530 of the geodetic second invariant unaccounted for) and then tested.

sources.title: Kostrov (1974), seismic moment / strain-rate summation
sources.used_for: Origin of the summation the fault-slip variant is built on.
sources.verified: SECOND-HAND (cited inside Kreemer et al. 2000, which is verified above)
sources.notes: No independent numeric use; included for completeness of the citation chain.

sources.title: Siler (2022), Slip- and dilation-tendency calculations for Quaternary faults of the Great Basin (USGS data release)
sources.used_for: Per-fault dips and strikes, used to justify the dip value in the Stage-A sum (and to show the dip distribution by slip sense).
sources.verified: OWNER (listing and DataCite record re-checked; data file obtained through the owner mirror and hash-pinned here)
sources.notes: CSV slice used here: work/sb_slip_tendency_in_footprint.csv (84,484 rows).
